tagline: Chicken Dinner Road and the orchards above the Snake.
intro: From Walters Ferry on Idaho 45 the byway turns off onto back roads, Map Rock Road and Chicken Dinner Road among them, and wanders north some fifty miles through farm country above the Snake River canyon to the bridge at Nyssa, Oregon.

Volcanoes laid this ground down millions of years ago, and about 15,000 years ago the Bonneville Flood, one of the largest in geologic history, ran through the whole valley. The pioneers found it sagebrush and made it into farms.
season: Visit Idaho calls it a drive for any time of year, with the orchards best seen in spring or in fall just before harvest.

moments.title: Sunnyslope Wine Trail
moments.text: Along these back roads the byway runs among the orchards and the vineyards of the Sunnyslope Wine Trail, in the state's wine-growing country.

moments.title: Homedale
moments.text: Homedale drew its name out of a hat at a community picnic, and the Austrians lured here in 1914 with promises of good farmland still have an Austrian Town.

moments.title: Parma
moments.text: Near Parma the Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Boise in 1834 by the mouth of the Boise River to rival Fort Hall, and kept it until 1854.
